title: Integer overflow of `+ - *` and negation
verdict: deviation: unbounded, and reported as a warning
description: DuckDB raises `Out of Range Error: Overflow …` at the declared width, `TINYINT` included, which is the reference (native). If a plan asks for `SILENT` or `SATURATE`, it needs a shim: compute in `HUGEINT` and wrap, `((x::HUGEINT + y + 2^(w-1)) % 2^w + 2^w) % 2^w - 2^(w-1)`, or clamp, `LEAST(GREATEST(x::HUGEINT + y, MIN_w), MAX_w)`, then cast back. `HUGEINT` holds every `i64` product, so both are exact. The written plan must emit the arithmetic at its declared width (S2 in the [README](README.md)).
Frontend (duckdb-F3): DuckDB gives an integer literal the narrowest type that holds it, so `100::TINYINT + 50` is an `i8` addition in DuckDB, and an `i64` one in DataFusion's plan.
The docs are silent on integer arithmetic raising at the operands' declared width: a docs gap.
reference: Substrait and the reference: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `negate` and `abs` on `i8`/`i16`/`i32`/`i64` return the same type; `divide` on integers overflows for `MIN / -1`. With `overflow` omitted, the reference raises when the result does not fit the declared type.

Lean, `+ - *` and negation: deviation. `Rel.eval`'s integers are unbounded, and `UnFn.wrap n`, which marks arithmetic narrower than 64 bits, is the identity ([`Expr.lean:134`](../../core/Sverify/Core/Expr.lean#L134)). `verify` reports the overflow only as a warning (`may wrap around`, not an error), and the parser accepts only `SILENT` for `+ - *` ([`Parse.lean:770`](../../SubstraitLean/Parse.lean#L770)). So `9223372036854775800 + 5000` and `100::TINYINT + 50::TINYINT` answer `9223372036854780800` and `150`, with no error, where the reference raises. The fix: report overflow at the declared width as an error, and accept `overflow: ERROR` (and the omitted option) rather than only `SILENT`.

provenance.notes: `overflow: ERROR` matches, under every setting. `sverify_dev.probe` runs the function at each signature on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the 64-bit bounds, 0.5, ±2.5, 1e308, ±inf, NaN, NULL), one row at a time from columns, under every combination of `error_on_division_by_zero` and `ieee_floating_point_ops`. Lean evaluates the Substrait call on the same rows once per candidate value of its option (`substrait-check --outcomes`), and the candidates whose outcomes all match are DuckDB's options. No input is -0.0 (duckdb-R14).
